segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְשַׁלְשֵׁל דְּפָנוֹת מִלְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה, אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים — פְּסוּלָה. מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה, אִם גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — כְּשֵׁרָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, כָּךְ מִלְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One who lowers the walls» of the sukka «from up downward, if» the lower edge of the wall is «three handbreadths above the ground,» the sukka is «unfit.» Since animals can enter through that space, it is not the wall of a fit sukka. However, if one constructs the wall from «down upward, if» the wall is «ten handbreadths high,» even if it does not reach the roofing, the sukka is «fit. Rabbi Yosei says: Just as» a wall built «from down upward» must be «ten handbreadths, so too,» in a case where one lowers the wall «from up downward,» it must be «ten handbreadths» in length. Regardless of its height off the ground, it is the wall of a fit sukka, as the legal status of a ten-handbreadth partition is that of a full-fledged partition in all areas of halakha.

moves.summary: walls lowered from above are unfit if three handbreadths off the ground; built from below, ten handbreadths suffice
R' Yosei: ten handbreadths suffice from above just as from below
